tay: New hire hit a CF Workers quickstart snag. Build ok, runtime fails: "ReferenceError: process is not defined" then "Error: Cannot find module 'net'". The app only uses fetch + JWT verify. Any rapid remediation?

bree: Likely a transitive dep dragging in node builtins (buffer/net/fs). Which jwt library?

tay: jwt-lite. Bundle analysis shows buffer pulled by a base64 helper.

oliver: Two pragmatic fixes: 1) swap to a web-first verifier that uses WebCrypto directly, 2) ship a tiny opt-in shim package with explicit worker-safe exports and node stubs that throw with clear guidance. We prefer opt-in so customers don't get surprising behavior.

oliver: Example guard for WebCrypto to include in the shim:
```js
export function ensureSubtle(){
  if (typeof globalThis.crypto?.subtle?.importKey !== 'function'){
    throw new Error('WebCrypto importKey not available in this runtime. See https://go.redwood.dev/edge-crypto for guidance')
  }
}
```

bree: For bundlers: make sure esbuild/WRANGLER target is service-worker and avoid auto-polyfills. Also use conditional exports in the package so bundlers pick a worker-specific entrypoint: 
```json
{"exports": {"./crypto": {"worker":"dist/crypto.worker.mjs","node":"dist/crypto.node.cjs"}}, "types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
That keeps node-only code out of worker builds when bundlers respect conditional exports.

tay: Typing problems: TS projects saw "Cannot find module '@redwood/inference-edge-shims'" when the shim lacked d.ts. What's the minimal types strategy?

oliver: Ship a small index.d.ts with the exported helpers and set `types` in package.json. Also add a sample tsconfig for worker consumers: 
```json
{"compilerOptions": {"lib":["es2021","webworker"], "moduleResolution":"bundler", "skipLibCheck": true}}
```
This reduces collisions between DOM and Node types.

bree: Auth retry nuance in Workers: no persistent sockets so refresh storms are a risk. Use a single-refresh promise stored on globalThis to serialize refreshes, then retry original request with a single refresh + up to 2 backoff retries. Pseudocode: 
```js
async function fetchWithAuth(url, opts){
  for (let attempt=0; attempt<3; attempt++){
    const res = await fetch(url, opts)
    if (res.status !== 401) return res
    if (attempt === 0) await refreshOnce() // uses globalThis mutex
    else await sleep((2**attempt)*100 + Math.random()*100)
  }
  throw new Error('auth failed after retries')
}
```

tay: CI failures: our integration runner executed worker tests in plain Node (no WebCrypto) and flaked. How do we test Workers reliably?

ci-bot: File created: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/1202 - add a Miniflare job for worker-targeted tests and mark tests that depend on webcrypto.

oliver: We'll add a Miniflare job to the GitHub Actions matrix and update the samples PR to run the worker suite there. Also add a lint rule to warn if package indicates `platform: worker` but imports known node-only modules (`fs`, `net`, `child_process`, `os`, `buffer`). Provide autofix suggestions where possible.

bree: Small UX detail: ship the shim with three entrypoints (mjs/cjs/worker) and a tiny README checklist: 1) node builtins (avoid or use shim), 2) webcrypto caveats (importKey support), 3) bundler target (service-worker), 4) tsconfig sample. That should cut onboarding friction significantly.

tay: Can someone open a quick PR for the shim + sample updates? New hires keep tripping on this.

devx-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/700 - adds `@redwood/inference-edge-shims` (dist: .mjs/.cjs/.worker.mjs) + index.d.ts + sample quickstart updates. CI pending with Miniflare job. :rocket:

tay: Thanks 44f this looks like it will make the CF onboarding much smoother.
